reasoning_traces.think:
The divergence operator D = money% - ticket% captures the relative weight of informed versus uninformed bets. When D > 0, sharp money dominates the ticket side, indicating contrarian positioning. This creates a dualistic view: model predictions vs. sharp money consensus. The correction mechanism arises when D deviates significantly from model expectations—such as in TEN +10.5 where divergence is +18. Here, sharp money contradicts the model’s injury-based edge, suggesting an external factor. The system must evaluate whether to trust the model or the sharp money, using D as a probabilistic signal. In CHI +3.5, both model and sharp money align, reinforcing confidence. The failure mode occurs when D is near zero, implying no meaningful signal. The epistemic structure thus combines Bayesian updating with empirical validation through observed D values.
